boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: A source-backed mix of current Flyer rituals and clearly labeled historical traditions from University of Dayton records.

cards.title: Christmas on Campus
cards.subtitle: Annual December celebration and student–child buddy event
cards.notes: Attend the public celebration, then look for the tree lighting, activity spaces and the Chapel Mass that follows the evening program.
cards.short_summary: A December campus tradition pairing Dayton schoolchildren with UD student buddies.
cards.evidence_claim: UD describes Christmas on Campus as an annual tradition celebrating Christmas and the Feast of the Immaculate Conception; it pairs Dayton City Schools children with UD students and is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Annual December event; consult the official event page for the current date and program.

cards.title: Red Scare
cards.subtitle: University of Dayton student basketball-support organization
cards.notes: Spot the organized student section at a Flyer game and use the athletics tradition page to identify Red Scare in the campus fan culture.
cards.short_summary: The student organization named by UD Athletics as its Flyer fanatics.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Athletics lists Red Scare among Flyer traditions and identifies it as a student organization of Flyer fanatics.
cards.access_notes: Follow current Athletics game information and student-ticket guidance before attending.

cards.title: Flyer Pep Band
cards.subtitle: Official University of Dayton basketball pep band
cards.notes: Listen for the band during a Flyer game and connect its performance with the official athletics page’s list of campus traditions.
cards.short_summary: The official pep band included in UD Athletics’ Flyer-traditions listing.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Athletics lists the Flyer Pep Band as an official site within its Flyer Traditions page.
cards.access_notes: See the Athletics calendar for performances connected to current games.

cards.title: UD Cheerleading
cards.subtitle: Two-squad cheer program in Flyer athletics
cards.notes: Watch for the cheer squads at a Flyer event and recognize the program as one of the traditions documented by UD Athletics.
cards.short_summary: The two-squad cheer program named on UD Athletics’ traditions page.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Athletics lists UD Cheerleading among Flyer traditions and states that the program consists of two cheerleading squads and mascot Rudy Flyer.
cards.access_notes: Game appearances vary; check the official Athletics schedule.

cards.title: Rudy Flyer
cards.subtitle: University of Dayton athletics mascot
cards.notes: Look for Rudy Flyer during official athletics events and use the traditions page for the mascot’s connection to the cheerleading program.
cards.short_summary: The mascot documented within UD Athletics’ Flyer-traditions page.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Athletics identifies Rudy Flyer as the mascot within its description of the UD cheerleading program on the Flyer Traditions page.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the event; confirm through official Athletics communications.

cards.title: The Dayton Flyers Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Official song credited to Anthony McCarthy and D. Herbert Abel
cards.notes: Learn the chorus from the official athletics page before a game, then listen for the song as part of the documented Flyer tradition.
cards.short_summary: The official school song presented on UD Athletics’ traditions page.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Athletics presents the Dayton Flyers Fight Song on its Flyer Traditions page and credits lyrics to Anthony McCarthy and D. Herbert Abel.
cards.access_notes: Use the official Athletics page for the published lyrics and credits.

cards.title: Freshman Beanies
cards.subtitle: Discontinued freshman-initiation custom of the 1940s–1960s
cards.notes: Treat this as archive history: view the magazine’s period image and account rather than attempting to recreate the mandatory beanie practice.
cards.short_summary: A discontinued initiation-era custom involving light-blue, red-billed caps.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Magazine reports that freshman initiation in the 1940s through 1960s included mandatory light-blue, red-billed beanies and other practices.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued historical tradition; not a current student activity.

cards.title: University of Dayton Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Discontinued celebration last held in 2000
cards.notes: Use the magazine account to trace the former mix of reunions, parade, dances, Mass and football rather than looking for a current event.
cards.short_summary: A former campus-wide homecoming celebration documented as ending in 2000.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Magazine reports that University of Dayton homecoming included events such as Mass, parades, reunions, dances and football, and that the last celebration was held in 2000.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued historical tradition; the source says the final celebration occurred in 2000.

cards.title: University of Dayton Military Ball
cards.subtitle: Historical social event begun in 1919
cards.notes: Read the archive-based magazine account for the event’s origins and its role in earlier UD social life; it is not presented as current.
cards.short_summary: A historical University of Dayton social event that began in 1919.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Magazine states that the University of Dayton Military Ball started in 1919 and was the institution’s social event of the year.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; the cited article describes past events only.

cards.title: May Queen Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Discontinued Marian devotion held on May 1
cards.notes: Explore this only through the historical record: the account describes a May 1 rosary procession and flower offering to the Immaculate Conception statue.
cards.short_summary: A former May 1 ceremony honoring Mary through a student-elected May Queen.
cards.evidence_claim: UD Magazine reports that UD began crowning a May Queen in honor of Mary in 1935; the May 1 ceremony included a rosary procession and flowers offered at the Statue of the Immaculate Conception.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued historical tradition; the source’s eligibility language reflects its 1935 context.
